subject.title: feat(workspace): add tiered bootstrap loading with configurable bootstrapTier

question: Should OpenClaw accept `agents.defaults.bootstrapTier` as a core config surface now, and if so should no-override subagent behavior be modeled as a legacy heuristic or as the `minimal` tier?
rationale: The source gap and implementation are clear, but the new config/default surface affects prompt context, session state, hook extras, and upgrade expectations in a way automation should not decide.

options.title: Sponsor after contract cleanup
options.body: Accept the focused tiered-bootstrap direction, but require the resolver/default semantics, docs, and upgrade notes to make the legacy no-override path explicit before merge.

options.title: Fold into broader bootstrap policy
options.body: Pause this PR and design one selector contract that covers tiering, per-session filtering, prompt pressure, and hook extras together.

options.title: Decline the new config knob
options.body: Keep the existing fixed filters and steer users toward current context controls such as `contextInjection`, bootstrap budgets, lightweight mode, and doctor guidance.

recommendation.title: Sponsor after contract cleanup
recommendation.body: Accept the focused tiered-bootstrap direction, but require the resolver/default semantics, docs, and upgrade notes to make the legacy no-override path explicit before merge.
